notes: A RULING RELABEL. bmdb 1890 batch a01 of the tier-A census (lua, mosquitto, pureftpd, mbedtls). Brandon's 2026-09-29 DCL13-C rulings: a signature, callback or function-pointer-slot constraint is not an exception (option (c)): a function whose non-const pointer parameter is fixed by a function-pointer slot it is visibly assigned to is TP with provenance tag `oracle-tag: interface-fixed signature: fn-pointer slot` (the relaxed profile scores it FP); const is shallow as in C, so a write through a pointer member of *p is not a write to *p, while an array or nested-struct member write is. Each row was re-derived by reading the pinned source: FP only where the function writes *p directly, through a local alias, by passing p (or &p->m, or an array member) to a function or macro whose parameter is pointer-to-non-const or cannot be resolved, or by storing p itself into an object that outlives the call; otherwise TP, tagged where the function's name is assigned to a function-pointer object, table entry or function-pointer parameter in the pinned source. A key with several flagged parameters is TP if at least one is unmodified; its reason names each. Keys aurora-lint 44af4205 no longer reports at the line were relabeled on the parameter the prior reason discussed (provenance says so). Two rows were left out and listed for the coordinator (a prototype with no body; a parameter whose pointee is a function type). 72 TP rows carry the tag; 16 rows stay FP, their reasons restated on a write basis. Blind slice: 20 seeded rows (seed 18901) re-labeled by a fresh reader without the prior verdict or reason, one of them left out as above; 0 of 19 disagreed. Counting basis: distinct (project, commit, file, line, rule) keys.
